unmapped_concepts.suggested_description: The concept that the primary obstacle to AI adoption is not the technology itself, but the inability of the workforce to acquire necessary new skills. It highlights the systemic challenge of reskilling millions of workers.
unmapped_concepts.concept: The report identifies skill gaps as the single largest barrier to business transformation, with 63% of employers citing it as a major issue, emphasizing the human-capital bottleneck in AI adoption.
unmapped_concepts.reason: This concept bridges the gap between technological capability and economic implementation, appearing as a central theme across all POV camps.
unmapped_concepts.Accelerationist Interpretation: Upskilling is a necessary investment to unlock the full productivity potential of AI, turning a bottleneck into a competitive advantage.
unmapped_concepts.Safetyist Interpretation: Upskilling is a safety requirement to ensure workers can effectively oversee and manage increasingly autonomous AI systems.
unmapped_concepts.Skeptic Interpretation: The focus on upskilling shifts the burden of technological change onto workers, ignoring the systemic responsibility of corporations to provide stable employment.

unmapped_concepts.Skeptic Interpretation: This shift documents the erosion of human-centric work and the potential for deskilling as machines take over more tasks.
